pages.text: $(#36f)Wetness$() is the setup effect. On its own it only slows you down; combined with another element it produces most of the mod's biggest reactions.$(br2)It stacks up to $(thing)5 levels$(). Each level costs $(thing)10 seconds$() of decay time, so a full soak lingers for a long while.

pages.title: How you get wet
pages.text: $(li)Swimming: $(thing)3 levels$() in shallow water, the full $(thing)5$() when fully submerged.$(li)Rain or snow: $()+1 level per 10 seconds, up to 5.$(li)A thrown $(thing)splash water bottle$(), $(thing)splash mundane$() or $(thing)splash thick$() potion: +1 level. Elemental mobs carry these and will throw them at you.$(li)Standing in a $(thing)steam cloud$(): the cloud condenses onto you.

pages.title: How it ends
pages.text: $(li)Lava, magma blocks, and lit campfires or furnaces nearby dry you out.$(li)Standing $(thing)in fire$() for 2 seconds clears everything.$(li)In a hot, clear, open-sky biome, drying happens twice as fast.$(li)Cold biomes slow drying by half.$(li)A single Fire attack of your own burns off wetness - see $(l:elementalcraft:reactions/steam)Steam$(/l).

pages.title: What wetness does to you
pages.text: $(li)You stop burning, and fire cannot re-light you.$(li)Incoming $(thing)Fire elemental damage is reduced by 10% per level$().$(li)You get hungrier: +0.5 exhaustion per level.$(li)You become a target for reactions. Every reaction in the next chapter that begins with 'while wet' now applies to you.$(br2)Water animals, anything in the Nether, and blacklisted mobs are immune.
